The paper considers a dual function radar and communication (DFRC) base station equipped with N movable antenna elements.
The transmitter area is quantized into M possible discrete positions for the MA elements, with a minimum distance of D_min between any two MA elements.
The paper introduces chance constraints to precisely control the impact of the dynamic RCS fluctuations on the sensing quality of service (QoS).
The optimization problem is formulated as a non-convex mixed integer non-linear program (MINLP) to minimize the total transmit power while ensuring the communication and sensing QoS requirements.
An iterative alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is proposed to obtain a high-quality suboptimal solution for the MINLP problem.
Numerical results show that the proposed MA-enhanced ISAC system can reduce the BS transmit power by up to 40% compared to baseline methods.
Expanding the transmitter area enhances the performance of the proposed scheme, but at the expense of increased computational complexity.
The proposed scheme demonstrates remarkable robustness to RCS fluctuations, outperforming baseline methods even under stricter sensing QoS requirements.
The paper models the channel between the MA elements and users using a uniform field response vector (FRV) and path weights following a complex Gaussian distribution.
For sensing, the paper adopts a mean square error (MSE) metric between the ideal and actual beam patterns as the performance metric.
The paper leverages semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation and Taylor approximation to tackle the non-convexities in the optimization problem.
The computational complexity of the proposed AO algorithm is shown to be polynomial in the number of users, MA elements, and candidate positions.
The paper considers two baseline schemes: one with fixed antenna positions and another employing antenna selection (AS) with a uniform planar array.
Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed MA-enabled ISAC system outperforms the baseline schemes in terms of transmit power savings, especially for stricter sensing QoS requirements.
Increasing the normalized transmitter area size from 1 to 3 can provide up to 35% power savings for the proposed scheme under relaxed sensing QoS requirements.
